# Gadfly — User Stories
> ✅ done (shipped & tested) · 🟡 partial · ⬜ planned. Every ✅ cites the test.

## Priority backlog
_Nothing recorded yet._


## Epic SA — Socratic platform: foundation
- **GAD-US-SA1 ⬜** As MindAttic, Gadfly is a reusable Socratic engine any app can embed, with today's personal introspection tool as one consumer of it.


## Epic SB — Socratic platform: the engine
- **GAD-US-SB1 ⬜** As an examiner, I can run an adaptive Socratic exam that probes a student's understanding of each concept, confronts contradictions in their own claims, and stops at mastery, aporia or the time budget.
- **GAD-US-SB2 ⬜** As an instructor, I get a per-concept report with quoted evidence, source citations and the judges' dissent, as a recommendation I finalize.


## Epic SC — Socratic platform: source material and grounding
- **GAD-US-SC1 ⬜** As an instructor, I upload my own source material and get an editable concept map and rubric that every question and judgment is grounded in, with citations.


## Epic SD — Socratic platform: hosted server and API
- **GAD-US-SD1 ⬜** As the platform, every live session runs server-side with its turns, judgments and events persisted in SQL Server, resumable after a disconnect.
- **GAD-US-SD2 ⬜** As a third-party app, I can create exams, launch sessions in an embedded room and receive results through a keyed API and webhooks.


## Epic SF — Socratic platform: customer and student accounts
- **GAD-US-SF1 ⬜** As a customer org admin, I invite instructors and students into my organization, each with a role, and nobody ever sees another organization's data.


## Epic SG — Socratic platform: exam web app
- **GAD-US-SG1 ⬜** As a student, I check my mic and camera, consent, and take a spoken exam with a talking examiner that listens and follows up on what I said.
- **GAD-US-SG2 ⬜** As an instructor, I build exams from my sources, assign them, review each session's transcript, scores and evidence, and finalize the grade.


## Epic SI — Socratic platform: integrity
- **GAD-US-SI1 ⬜** As an instructor, I see integrity evidence (faces, voices, off-screen reading, focus loss, answer cadence) explained on the session timeline, with no automated accusation and no deception or emotion inference.


## Epic SP — Socratic platform: production and pilot
- **GAD-US-SP1 ⬜** As MindAttic, the platform runs on Azure with consent, retention, security and cost controls, and has been piloted with Erin's real exams.


## Epic MP — Master plan MVP: Socratic assessment with human-AI grading
- **GAD-US-MP1 ⬜** As an institution, I run adaptive Socratic examinations whose every response is verified and preserved, scored by AI per learning objective and independently by a human, reconciled when they disagree, combined by an approved weighting policy, and released only after authorized approval (docs/MASTER-PLAN.md).

| GAD-T73 | 2026-11-20 | fix | closed | HttpTenantContext reports IsSystem=true whenever IHttpContextAccessor.HttpContext is null, which turns off the tenant query filter and the write guard. Inside an interactive Blazor Server circuit HttpContext is not guaranteed (null on long-polling/SSE transports, timers, background continuations), so component queries could run unfiltered. Pin the tenant at circuit start from the AuthenticationStateProvider, fall back to 'no tenant' (sees nothing) instead of system, and make system an explicit opt-in for background scopes (GAD-T64 security review). | 77e3c46 |
| GAD-T74 | 2026-11-20 | fix | closed | SessionOrchestrator's live-session cache only compared the organization, so any student in the same organization who knew a session id could read its question, answer into it or end it via the hub/exam room before the ownership check in PersistAsync ran (the in-memory engine was already changed). Check the student on the cached path and before broadcasting Thinking (GAD-T64 security review). | 5c3df94 |
| GAD-T75 | 2026-11-20 | fix | closed | Webhook URLs only had to be https, so an org admin or API key could point deliveries at localhost, private ranges, link-local/metadata addresses or internal hostnames (blind SSRF with the response code shown as an oracle; redirects followed). Refuse non-public targets at registration and at connect time (DNS-rebinding safe) and stop following redirects (GAD-T64 security review). | dbc4c17 |
| GAD-T76 | 2026-11-20 | fix | closed | Organization memberships ride on the sign-in cookie, so removing a member or changing their role only took effect at their next sign-in, and an Admin could demote or deactivate an Owner (and so leave the organization ownerless). a111a80 Response analysis and evidence collection: every answer gets a panel analysis (claims, misconceptions per objective, uncertainties, evidence for/against each objective with its Part 5.1 dimension, whether the question revealed the answer), each reply validated strictly against the schema (exact keys, types, enums, known objectives; 92f679a Questioning strategies A-H: CausalReasoning, ScenarioVariation, AssumptionTesting and IndependentExplanation join conceptual probing, counterexample, transfer and contradiction; the planner picks by information value (the move whose answer best separates the corroborated level, the tentative top and the plausible ceiling, with misconception, dimension-gap, repetition and difficulty terms) and records why; the question prompt (ExamPromptsV3, merged as the next prompt-set version until folded into ExamPrompts) describes all eight and forbids teaching in examination mode; Learning Mode hints and guided explanations get their own prompt; one implicit objective per concept when an exam has none); per objective a deterministic assessor tracks corroboration (a level needs 2+ independent supporting answers, a conclusion 2+ independent answers), consistency (unconfronted or failed contradictions), transfer and critical reasoning shown, untested misconceptions and remaining uncertainty, and closes it as Sufficient or Inconclusive (per-objective question limit, time with the accommodations multiplier, turn limit, leaving room for unstarted objectives), reporting Level 0 Insufficient Evidence instead of guessing; 95 vs 60 opens a mandatory disagreement that blocks approval and publication until a second reviewer documents the resolution; students, examiners and second reviewers are refused amending, scoring, approving or publishing, the grade is untouched and every attempt is an access.denied audit event, while an instructor's amendment goes through (GAD-T101); e0426be Assessment report (Feature 10): final grade, per-objective AI, human and combined scores, verified evidence quotes, knowledge gaps, approval and appeal history, MOCK and preliminary labels; reviewer view at /grading/{id}/report with Markdown and CSV export, student view at /my-results/{id} only after approval and publication, with the appeal form and a Markdown download (GAD-T99); 75567b2 Human grading, combined scoring, reconciliation and final approval (Parts 8-11): grading queue and workspace for Examiners/Teachers (transcript with verified and original text, versions, verification and clarification history, objectives and rubrics, evidence, AI grades with flags and each voter); blind mode hides AI grades and their audit entries until the human submits every objective; HumanObjectiveGrade per objective (adjustments supersede, WasBlind kept); CombinedScoring under the frozen policy and objective weights, a GradeDisagreement per objective, Reconciliation Required blocks finalization (rechecked at approval); side-by-side reconciliation with cause, resolution, resolved scores, second reviewer and recalculation; approve (Finalize record), publish, student appeal, uphold/dismiss or amend; PermissionMatrix on every action with refusals audited; the old release-results path retired so nothing reaches a student without an approval record (GAD-T98); c131f80 Test host never touches live LLM providers (Gadfly:AiMode=mock, so the startup panel probe stays offline); the scripted panel recognizes the v3 objective question, learning-mode and response-analysis prompts (GAD-T104); 08e6689 AI preliminary grading per objective (Part 7, Component F): when a session ends a sweeper creates its FinalGrade and queues grading.ai; the job backfills immutable StudentResponse records from stored answers, holds at Transcript Verification Pending while a response needs a human, freezes the grading policy, derives one objective per examined concept when the exam has none (audited), and grades each objective with the panel: schema-validated levels 0-5 per rubric criterion citing numbered verified responses only (uncited levels refused, citations outside the evidence dropped, quotes kept only if verbatim), scores computed in code (Level-0 criteria left out, not zeroed), median across voters with dissent recorded, misconceptions, ambiguities, review flags, an evidence-criteria confidence category and IsMock from IPanelInfo; AiObjectiveGrade rows, every status move through GradeStatusMachine and audited (GAD-T94); a996dc1 Exhaustive tests: organization-role policies, every role against OrgAdmin/Instructor/Student/Member/Api, the staff MFA rule and its development override, no organization or role refused, examiners and second reviewers are members but not instructors or admins (GAD-T104); f930fd0 Fix the level-0 descriptor test: the descriptor says the examination 'does not provide enough reliable evidence', so the test looks for 'enough reliable evidence' (GAD-T108); e9bbeea Master plan Part 20 scenarios A-J as named tests: A (a correct definition earns no mastery, follow-ups come), B (the initial error and later reasoning both stay in the evidence), C (unclear answers get a Clarify move; drafts that teach are replaced, interpretation-offering clarifications fall back to the student's own words), D (transcript correction keeps the original, scores the verified text, audited), E (a substantive revision is a new response row pointing at the original, with the exam's rule), F (agreement combines and waits for approval), G (95 vs 60 must reconcile, no automatic finalization), H (turn and time limits end without invented certainty; split judges go to a human), I (leaking questions are guarded and replaced), J (unauthorized grade changes are refused and logged as access.denied, cross-organization writes blocked); contamination exclusion waits on GAD-T92 (GAD-T101); 1383e71 Exhaustive tests, part 2: an in-process Gadfly.Server (WebApplicationFactory) on a uniquely named LocalDB database migrated by the app and dropped after the run, with a scripted panel, a manual clock and background services off; tenant filter on every tenant-owned table and isolation across the exam chain, write guard (add/modify/delete/move across organizations, nobody, system), append-only audit and immutable original responses, membership claim parsing; organization directory rules (roles, owner protection, last owner, outside accounts, security-stamp rotation); retention redaction keeps scores and removes words, export content and scoping, erasure; session orchestrator create/resume/window/attempts/quota/consent/ownership/time limit and grace/restart resume/pinned subject/persistence; webhook SSRF table, signature, outbox staging, give-up on bad targets; API key shape, hashing, revocation; usage pricing, cost staging and monthly quota; every mapped route default-deny against the anonymous allow-list; platform API authentication, validation (400/404/409), tenant scoping, launch tokens and the 429 rate limit (GAD-T104); 7cd98b0 Wire the AI panel selection (live / clearly labelled mock / auto), startup panel decision, --seed-demo, the MOCK banner on every layout, and the verification backfill (GAD-T100); a371a49 Exam room confirmation and correction: a pending clarification or transcript check shows inline, one at a time, under the question with the answer as recorded (Yes / correct it / repeat for transcripts; reply, decline or fix a typo instead for meaning), with wording that confirming the transcript is not confirming correctness; after each answer, 'Correct a typo in my last answer' (a transcription correction, original kept, never a penalty) and 'I want to change my answer' (a new response event, shown with the exam's revision rule); time running out during a request submits the answer as recorded for human review (GAD-T88); 1d55911 Verification engine and neutral clarification: after each answer, deterministic checks (incomplete sentence, explicit student request, low speech confidence) plus a schema-checked panel vote decide whether the uncertainty could materially change grading; a clarification is worded by a dedicated prompt that forbids technical content, then must pass a no-new-terms check, a no-interpretation-offered check and the LEAKS/SAFE guard, else a template quoting only the student; voice answers get transcript confirmation first; the orchestrator holds judging until the student replies (pending state persisted, resumes after restart), judges the verified text plus the clarification, sends declined/expired/over-budget ambiguity to human review, and exposes Verification, LastAnswer and Notice on SessionStep with hub methods Clarify, ConfirmTranscript, CorrectAnswer and ReviseAnswer; typo fixes are bounded by deterministic correction rules; exam prompt set v3 (GAD-T87); 94bfb23 Response versioning services: every answer is an immutable StudentResponse (original text, modality, Captured) with transcript version 1 and a capture audit event carrying its timings; transcription corrections add versions and update the verified text, meaning clarifications are stored beside the original, substantive revisions are new response rows pointing at what they revise; every state change goes through VerificationMachine as a ResponseVerification row plus an AuditEvent; earlier answered turns are backfilled as Captured originals by a startup service (AddVerification) (GAD-T86); 69b12b8 Demo tour (Gadfly.Tour): starts a real Gadfly.Server under a renamed exe in mock (or --live) mode against a throwaway LocalDB database (--fresh), seeds the demo, and drives the workflow as real users over HTTP, the platform API and the SessionHub (antiforgery sign-in for every role, MOCK banner, access control, teacher setup, API source processing, student exam with good/ambiguous/typo/revision/I-don't-know answers, end and report, mock labelling, AI and human grading, approval, appeal, report export, review, API results, analytics, audit); every stage asserts against the API and database and prints a checklist, unbuilt features SKIP with their ticket by probing hub methods, routes and tables; exit 1 on any failure; docs/TOUR.md (GAD-T105)) | 84f3cc1 |

side-by-side reconciliation with cause, resolution, resolved scores, second reviewer and recalculation; approve (Finalize record), publish, student appeal, uphold/dismiss or amend; PermissionMatrix on every action with refusals audited; the old release-results path retired so nothing reaches a student without an approval record (GAD-T98); c131f80 Test host never touches live LLM providers (Gadfly:AiMode=mock, so the startup panel probe stays offline); the scripted panel recognizes the v3 objective question, learning-mode and response-analysis prompts (GAD-T104); 08e6689 AI preliminary grading per objective (Part 7, Component F): when a session ends a sweeper creates its FinalGrade and queues grading.ai; tenant filter on every tenant-owned table and isolation across the exam chain, write guard (add/modify/delete/move across organizations, nobody, system), append-only audit and immutable original responses, membership claim parsing; organization directory rules (roles, owner protection, last owner, outside accounts, security-stamp rotation); retention redaction keeps scores and removes words, export content and scoping, erasure; session orchestrator create/resume/window/attempts/quota/consent/ownership/time limit and grace/restart resume/pinned subject/persistence; webhook SSRF table, signature, outbox staging, give-up on bad targets; 7cd98b0 Wire the AI panel selection (live / clearly labelled mock / auto), startup panel decision, --seed-demo, the MOCK banner on every layout, and the verification backfill (GAD-T100); a371a49 Exam room confirmation and correction: a pending clarification or transcript check shows inline, one at a time, under the question with the answer as recorded (Yes / correct it / repeat for transcripts; voice answers get transcript confirmation first; the orchestrator holds judging until the student replies (pending state persisted, resumes after restart), judges the verified text plus the clarification, sends declined/expired/over-budget ambiguity to human review, and exposes Verification, LastAnswer and Notice on SessionStep with hub methods Clarify, ConfirmTranscript, CorrectAnswer and ReviseAnswer; typo fixes are bounded by deterministic correction rules; exam prompt set v3 (GAD-T87); 94bfb23 Response versioning services: every answer is an immutable StudentResponse (original text, modality, Captured) with transcript version 1 and a capture audit event carrying its timings; transcription corrections add versions and update the verified text, meaning clarifications are stored beside the original, substantive revisions are new response rows pointing at what they revise; every state change goes through VerificationMachine as a ResponseVerification row plus an AuditEvent; earlier answered turns are backfilled as Captured originals by a startup service (AddVerification) (GAD-T86); 69b12b8 Demo tour (Gadfly.Tour): starts a real Gadfly.Server under a renamed exe in mock (or --live) mode against a throwaway LocalDB database (--fresh), seeds the demo, and drives the workflow as real users over HTTP, the platform API and the SessionHub (antiforgery sign-in for every role, MOCK banner, access control, teacher setup, API source processing, student exam with good/ambiguous/typo/revision/I-don't-know answers, end and report, mock labelling, AI and human grading, approval, appeal, report export, review, API results, analytics, audit); a111a80 Response analysis and evidence collection: every answer gets a panel analysis (claims, misconceptions per objective, uncertainties, evidence for/against each objective with its Part 5.1 dimension, whether the question revealed the answer), each reply validated strictly against the schema (exact keys, types, enums, known objectives; malformed replies rejected with the reason recorded), items whose quote is not the student's own words dropped, the rest merged by majority; analysis claims feed the claim ledger; an honest "I don't know" is analysed deterministically; SourceExamEngine exposes Objectives, Assessments(), CollectEvidence(), FlagLeak() and CheckClarificationAsync(); EvidenceWriter maps the engine's evidence to AssessmentEvidence rows linked to the verified response and its latest transcript version (verbatim-quote and verified-state checks, idempotent, contamination/assistance flags only turn on, audited) (GAD-T91); 92f679a Questioning strategies A-H: CausalReasoning, ScenarioVariation, AssumptionTesting and IndependentExplanation join conceptual probing, counterexample, transfer and contradiction; the planner picks by information value (the move whose answer best separates the corroborated level, the tentative top and the plausible ceiling, with misconception, dimension-gap, repetition and difficulty terms) and records why; the question prompt (ExamPromptsV3, merged as the next prompt-set version until folded into ExamPrompts) describes all eight and forbids teaching in examination mode; Learning Mode hints and guided explanations get their own prompt; the leak guard fails closed (undecided -> safe fallback) and is reusable on clarifications; drafts that are only a move name or talk about the student are not asked (GAD-T90); 14bc148 Objective-driven examination control: the engine examines learning objectives (key, title, grounding concepts, rubric criteria/dimensions; one implicit objective per concept when an exam has none); per objective a deterministic assessor tracks corroboration (a level needs 2+ independent supporting answers, a conclusion 2+ independent answers), consistency (unconfronted or failed contradictions), transfer and critical reasoning shown, untested misconceptions and remaining uncertainty, and closes it as Sufficient or Inconclusive (per-objective question limit, time with the accommodations multiplier, turn limit, leaving room for unstarted objectives), reporting Level 0 Insufficient Evidence instead of guessing; contaminated answers (after a leaked question) and assisted answers (after a Learning Mode hint) never count as independent; the session ends EvidenceComplete; the report gains per-objective levels and Level 0 notices (GAD-T89); e84a96d Wire the grading pipeline (services, sweeper, report endpoints) and a Grading nav link for owners, admins, instructors, examiners and second reviewers (GAD-T98); 80f225e Scenarios F, G and J through the real grading workflow on LocalDB: agreement combines to 86.8 and waits for approval (the examiner can't approve, the instructor finalizes and publishes); 95 vs 60 opens a mandatory disagreement that blocks approval and publication until a second reviewer documents the resolution; students, examiners and second reviewers are refused amending, scoring, approving or publishing, the grade is untouched and every attempt is an access.denied audit event, while an instructor's amendment goes through (GAD-T101); e0426be Assessment report (Feature 10): final grade, per-objective AI, human and combined scores, verified evidence quotes, knowledge gaps, approval and appeal history, MOCK and preliminary labels; reviewer view at /grading/{id}/report with Markdown and CSV export, student view at /my-results/{id} only after approval and publication, with the appeal form and a Markdown download (GAD-T99); 75567b2 Human grading, combined scoring, reconciliation and final approval (Parts 8-11): grading queue and workspace for Examiners/Teachers (transcript with verified and original text, versions, verification and clarification history, objectives and rubrics, evidence, AI grades with flags and each voter); blind mode hides AI grades and their audit entries until the human submits every objective; HumanObjectiveGrade per objective (adjustments supersede, WasBlind kept); CombinedScoring under the frozen policy and objective weights, a GradeDisagreement per objective, Reconciliation Required blocks finalization (rechecked at approval); side-by-side reconciliation with cause, resolution, resolved scores, second reviewer and recalculation; approve (Finalize record), publish, student appeal, uphold/dismiss or amend; PermissionMatrix on every action with refusals audited; the old release-results path retired so nothing reaches a student without an approval record (GAD-T98); c131f80 Test host never touches live LLM providers (Gadfly:AiMode=mock, so the startup panel probe stays offline); the scripted panel recognizes the v3 objective question, learning-mode and response-analysis prompts (GAD-T104); 08e6689 AI preliminary grading per objective (Part 7, Component F): when a session ends a sweeper creates its FinalGrade and queues grading.ai; the job backfills immutable StudentResponse records from stored answers, holds at Transcript Verification Pending while a response needs a human, freezes the grading policy, derives one objective per examined concept when the exam has none (audited), and grades each objective with the panel: schema-validated levels 0-5 per rubric criterion citing numbered verified responses only (uncited levels refused, citations outside the evidence dropped, quotes kept only if verbatim), scores computed in code (Level-0 criteria left out, not zeroed), median across voters with dissent recorded, misconceptions, ambiguities, review flags, an evidence-criteria confidence category and IsMock from IPanelInfo; AiObjectiveGrade rows, every status move through GradeStatusMachine and audited (GAD-T94); a996dc1 Exhaustive tests: organization-role policies, every role against OrgAdmin/Instructor/Student/Member/Api, the staff MFA rule and its development override, no organization or role refused, examiners and second reviewers are members but not instructors or admins (GAD-T104); f930fd0 Fix the level-0 descriptor test: the descriptor says the examination 'does not provide enough reliable evidence', so the test looks for 'enough reliable evidence' (GAD-T108); e9bbeea Master plan Part 20 scenarios A-J as named tests: A (a correct definition earns no mastery, follow-ups come), B (the initial error and later reasoning both stay in the evidence), C (unclear answers get a Clarify move; drafts that teach are replaced, interpretation-offering clarifications fall back to the student's own words), D (transcript correction keeps the original, scores the verified text, audited), E (a substantive revision is a new response row pointing at the original, with the exam's rule), F (agreement combines and waits for approval), G (95 vs 60 must reconcile, no automatic finalization), H (turn and time limits end without invented certainty; split judges go to a human), I (leaking questions are guarded and replaced), J (unauthorized grade changes are refused and logged as access.denied, cross-organization writes blocked); contamination exclusion waits on GAD-T92 (GAD-T101); 1383e71 Exhaustive tests, part 2: an in-process Gadfly.Server (WebApplicationFactory) on a uniquely named LocalDB database migrated by the app and dropped after the run, with a scripted panel, a manual clock and background services off; tenant filter on every tenant-owned table and isolation across the exam chain, write guard (add/modify/delete/move across organizations, nobody, system), append-only audit and immutable original responses, membership claim parsing; organization directory rules (roles, owner protection, last owner, outside accounts, security-stamp rotation); retention redaction keeps scores and removes words, export content and scoping, erasure; session orchestrator create/resume/window/attempts/quota/consent/ownership/time limit and grace/restart resume/pinned subject/persistence; webhook SSRF table, signature, outbox staging, give-up on bad targets; API key shape, hashing, revocation; usage pricing, cost staging and monthly quota; every mapped route default-deny against the anonymous allow-list; platform API authentication, validation (400/404/409), tenant scoping, launch tokens and the 429 rate limit (GAD-T104); 7cd98b0 Wire the AI panel selection (live / clearly labelled mock / auto), startup panel decision, --seed-demo, the MOCK banner on every layout, and the verification backfill (GAD-T100); a371a49 Exam room confirmation and correction: a pending clarification or transcript check shows inline, one at a time, under the question with the answer as recorded (Yes / correct it / repeat for transcripts; reply, decline or fix a typo instead for meaning), with wording that confirming the transcript is not confirming correctness; after each answer, 'Correct a typo in my last answer' (a transcription correction, original kept, never a penalty) and 'I want to change my answer' (a new response event, shown with the exam's revision rule); time running out during a request submits the answer as recorded for human review (GAD-T88); 1d55911 Verification engine and neutral clarification: after each answer, deterministic checks (incomplete sentence, explicit student request, low speech confidence) plus a schema-checked panel vote decide whether the uncertainty could materially change grading; a clarification is worded by a dedicated prompt that forbids technical content, then must pass a no-new-terms check, a no-interpretation-offered check and the LEAKS/SAFE guard, else a template quoting only the student; voice answers get transcript confirmation first; the orchestrator holds judging until the student replies (pending state persisted, resumes after restart), judges the verified text plus the clarification, sends declined/expired/over-budget ambiguity to human review, and exposes Verification, LastAnswer and Notice on SessionStep with hub methods Clarify, ConfirmTranscript, CorrectAnswer and ReviseAnswer; typo fixes are bounded by deterministic correction rules; exam prompt set v3 (GAD-T87); 94bfb23 Response versioning services: every answer is an immutable StudentResponse (original text, modality, Captured) with transcript version 1 and a capture audit event carrying its timings; transcription corrections add versions and update the verified text, meaning clarifications are stored beside the original, substantive revisions are new response rows pointing at what they revise; every state change goes through VerificationMachine as a ResponseVerification row plus an AuditEvent; earlier answered turns are backfilled as Captured originals by a startup service (AddVerification) (GAD-T86); 69b12b8 Demo tour (Gadfly.Tour): starts a real Gadfly.Server under a renamed exe in mock (or --live) mode against a throwaway LocalDB database (--fresh), seeds the demo, and drives the workflow as real users over HTTP, the platform API and the SessionHub (antiforgery sign-in for every role, MOCK banner, access control, teacher setup, API source processing, student exam with good/ambiguous/typo/revision/I-don't-know answers, end and report, mock labelling, AI and human grading, approval, appeal, report export, review, API results, analytics, audit); every stage asserts against the API and database and prints a checklist, unbuilt features SKIP with their ticket by probing hub methods, routes and tables; exit 1 on any failure; docs/TOUR.md (GAD-T105)) | bce163c |

time running out during a request submits the answer as recorded for human review (GAD-T88); 1d55911 Verification engine and neutral clarification: after each answer, deterministic checks (incomplete sentence, explicit student request, low speech confidence) plus a schema-checked panel vote decide whether the uncertainty could materially change grading; a clarification is worded by a dedicated prompt that forbids technical content, then must pass a no-new-terms check, a no-interpretation-offered check and the LEAKS/SAFE guard, else a template quoting only the student; voice answers get transcript confirmation first; the orchestrator holds judging until the student replies (pending state persisted, resumes after restart), judges the verified text plus the clarification, sends declined/expired/over-budget ambiguity to human review, and exposes Verification, LastAnswer and Notice on SessionStep with hub methods Clarify, ConfirmTranscript, CorrectAnswer and ReviseAnswer; typo fixes are bounded by deterministic correction rules; exam prompt set v3 (GAD-T87); 94bfb23 Response versioning services: every answer is an immutable StudentResponse (original text, modality, Captured) with transcript version 1 and a capture audit event carrying its timings; transcription corrections add versions and update the verified text, meaning clarifications are stored beside the original, substantive revisions are new response rows pointing at what they revise; every state change goes through VerificationMachine as a ResponseVerification row plus an AuditEvent; earlier answered turns are backfilled as Captured originals by a startup service (AddVerification) (GAD-T86); 69b12b8 Demo tour (Gadfly.Tour): starts a real Gadfly.Server under a renamed exe in mock (or --live) mode against a throwaway LocalDB database (--fresh), seeds the demo, and drives the workflow as real users over HTTP, the platform API and the SessionHub (antiforgery sign-in for every role, MOCK banner, access control, teacher setup, API source processing, student exam with good/ambiguous/typo/revision/I-don't-know answers, end and report, mock labelling, AI and human grading, approval, appeal, report export, review, API results, analytics, audit); every stage asserts against the API and database and prints a checklist, unbuilt features SKIP with their ticket by probing hub methods, routes and tables; exit 1 on any failure; docs/TOUR.md (GAD-T105)) | 84f3cc1 |

tenant filter on every tenant-owned table and isolation across the exam chain, write guard (add/modify/delete/move across organizations, nobody, system), append-only audit and immutable original responses, membership claim parsing; organization directory rules (roles, owner protection, last owner, outside accounts, security-stamp rotation); retention redaction keeps scores and removes words, export content and scoping, erasure; session orchestrator create/resume/window/attempts/quota/consent/ownership/time limit and grace/restart resume/pinned subject/persistence; webhook SSRF table, signature, outbox staging, give-up on bad targets; API key shape, hashing, revocation; usage pricing, cost staging and monthly quota; every mapped route default-deny against the anonymous allow-list; platform API authentication, validation (400/404/409), tenant scoping, launch tokens and the 429 rate limit (GAD-T104); 7cd98b0 Wire the AI panel selection (live / clearly labelled mock / auto), startup panel decision, --seed-demo, the MOCK banner on every layout, and the verification backfill (GAD-T100); a371a49 Exam room confirmation and correction: a pending clarification or transcript check shows inline, one at a time, under the question with the answer as recorded (Yes / correct it / repeat for transcripts; reply, decline or fix a typo instead for meaning), with wording that confirming the transcript is not confirming correctness; after each answer, 'Correct a typo in my last answer' (a transcription correction, original kept, never a penalty) and 'I want to change my answer' (a new response event, shown with the exam's revision rule); time running out during a request submits the answer as recorded for human review (GAD-T88); 1d55911 Verification engine and neutral clarification: after each answer, deterministic checks (incomplete sentence, explicit student request, low speech confidence) plus a schema-checked panel vote decide whether the uncertainty could materially change grading; a clarification is worded by a dedicated prompt that forbids technical content, then must pass a no-new-terms check, a no-interpretation-offered check and the LEAKS/SAFE guard, else a template quoting only the student; voice answers get transcript confirmation first; the orchestrator holds judging until the student replies (pending state persisted, resumes after restart), judges the verified text plus the clarification, sends declined/expired/over-budget ambiguity to human review, and exposes Verification, LastAnswer and Notice on SessionStep with hub methods Clarify, ConfirmTranscript, CorrectAnswer and ReviseAnswer; typo fixes are bounded by deterministic correction rules; exam prompt set v3 (GAD-T87); 94bfb23 Response versioning services: every answer is an immutable StudentResponse (original text, modality, Captured) with transcript version 1 and a capture audit event carrying its timings; transcription corrections add versions and update the verified text, meaning clarifications are stored beside the original, substantive revisions are new response rows pointing at what they revise; every state change goes through VerificationMachine as a ResponseVerification row plus an AuditEvent; earlier answered turns are backfilled as Captured originals by a startup service (AddVerification) (GAD-T86); 69b12b8 Demo tour (Gadfly.Tour): starts a real Gadfly.Server under a renamed exe in mock (or --live) mode against a throwaway LocalDB database (--fresh), seeds the demo, and drives the workflow as real users over HTTP, the platform API and the SessionHub (antiforgery sign-in for every role, MOCK banner, access control, teacher setup, API source processing, student exam with good/ambiguous/typo/revision/I-don't-know answers, end and report, mock labelling, AI and human grading, approval, appeal, report export, review, API results, analytics, audit); the leak guard fails closed (undecided -> safe fallback) and is reusable on clarifications; drafts that are only a move name or talk about the student are not asked (GAD-T90); 14bc148 Objective-driven examination control: the engine examines learning objectives (key, title, grounding concepts, rubric criteria/dimensions; one implicit objective per concept when an exam has none); per objective a deterministic assessor tracks corroboration (a level needs 2+ independent supporting answers, a conclusion 2+ independent answers), consistency (unconfronted or failed contradictions), transfer and critical reasoning shown, untested misconceptions and remaining uncertainty, and closes it as Sufficient or Inconclusive (per-objective question limit, time with the accommodations multiplier, turn limit, leaving room for unstarted objectives), reporting Level 0 Insufficient Evidence instead of guessing; contaminated answers (after a leaked question) and assisted answers (after a Learning Mode hint) never count as independent; the session ends EvidenceComplete; the report gains per-objective levels and Level 0 notices (GAD-T89); e84a96d Wire the grading pipeline (services, sweeper, report endpoints) and a Grading nav link for owners, admins, instructors, examiners and second reviewers (GAD-T98); 80f225e Scenarios F, G and J through the real grading workflow on LocalDB: agreement combines to 86.8 and waits for approval (the examiner can't approve, the instructor finalizes and publishes); 95 vs 60 opens a mandatory disagreement that blocks approval and publication until a second reviewer documents the resolution; students, examiners and second reviewers are refused amending, scoring, approving or publishing, the grade is untouched and every attempt is an access.denied audit event, while an instructor's amendment goes through (GAD-T101); e0426be Assessment report (Feature 10): final grade, per-objective AI, human and combined scores, verified evidence quotes, knowledge gaps, approval and appeal history, MOCK and preliminary labels; reviewer view at /grading/{id}/report with Markdown and CSV export, student view at /my-results/{id} only after approval and publication, with the appeal form and a Markdown download (GAD-T99); 75567b2 Human grading, combined scoring, reconciliation and final approval (Parts 8-11): grading queue and workspace for Examiners/Teachers (transcript with verified and original text, versions, verification and clarification history, objectives and rubrics, evidence, AI grades with flags and each voter); blind mode hides AI grades and their audit entries until the human submits every objective; HumanObjectiveGrade per objective (adjustments supersede, WasBlind kept); CombinedScoring under the frozen policy and objective weights, a GradeDisagreement per objective, Reconciliation Required blocks finalization (rechecked at approval); side-by-side reconciliation with cause, resolution, resolved scores, second reviewer and recalculation; approve (Finalize record), publish, student appeal, uphold/dismiss or amend; PermissionMatrix on every action with refusals audited; the old release-results path retired so nothing reaches a student without an approval record (GAD-T98); c131f80 Test host never touches live LLM providers (Gadfly:AiMode=mock, so the startup panel probe stays offline); the scripted panel recognizes the v3 objective question, learning-mode and response-analysis prompts (GAD-T104); 08e6689 AI preliminary grading per objective (Part 7, Component F): when a session ends a sweeper creates its FinalGrade and queues grading.ai; the job backfills immutable StudentResponse records from stored answers, holds at Transcript Verification Pending while a response needs a human, freezes the grading policy, derives one objective per examined concept when the exam has none (audited), and grades each objective with the panel: schema-validated levels 0-5 per rubric criterion citing numbered verified responses only (uncited levels refused, citations outside the evidence dropped, quotes kept only if verbatim), scores computed in code (Level-0 criteria left out, not zeroed), median across voters with dissent recorded, misconceptions, ambiguities, review flags, an evidence-criteria confidence category and IsMock from IPanelInfo; AiObjectiveGrade rows, every status move through GradeStatusMachine and audited (GAD-T94); a996dc1 Exhaustive tests: organization-role policies, every role against OrgAdmin/Instructor/Student/Member/Api, the staff MFA rule and its development override, no organization or role refused, examiners and second reviewers are members but not instructors or admins (GAD-T104); f930fd0 Fix the level-0 descriptor test: the descriptor says the examination 'does not provide enough reliable evidence', so the test looks for 'enough reliable evidence' (GAD-T108); e9bbeea Master plan Part 20 scenarios A-J as named tests: A (a correct definition earns no mastery, follow-ups come), B (the initial error and later reasoning both stay in the evidence), C (unclear answers get a Clarify move; drafts that teach are replaced, interpretation-offering clarifications fall back to the student's own words), D (transcript correction keeps the original, scores the verified text, audited), E (a substantive revision is a new response row pointing at the original, with the exam's rule), F (agreement combines and waits for approval), G (95 vs 60 must reconcile, no automatic finalization), H (turn and time limits end without invented certainty; split judges go to a human), I (leaking questions are guarded and replaced), J (unauthorized grade changes are refused and logged as access.denied, cross-organization writes blocked); contamination exclusion waits on GAD-T92 (GAD-T101); 1383e71 Exhaustive tests, part 2: an in-process Gadfly.Server (WebApplicationFactory) on a uniquely named LocalDB database migrated by the app and dropped after the run, with a scripted panel, a manual clock and background services off; tenant filter on every tenant-owned table and isolation across the exam chain, write guard (add/modify/delete/move across organizations, nobody, system), append-only audit and immutable original responses, membership claim parsing; organization directory rules (roles, owner protection, last owner, outside accounts, security-stamp rotation); retention redaction keeps scores and removes words, export content and scoping, erasure; session orchestrator create/resume/window/attempts/quota/consent/ownership/time limit and grace/restart resume/pinned subject/persistence; webhook SSRF table, signature, outbox staging, give-up on bad targets; API key shape, hashing, revocation; usage pricing, cost staging and monthly quota; every mapped route default-deny against the anonymous allow-list; platform API authentication, validation (400/404/409), tenant scoping, launch tokens and the 429 rate limit (GAD-T104); 7cd98b0 Wire the AI panel selection (live / clearly labelled mock / auto), startup panel decision, --seed-demo, the MOCK banner on every layout, and the verification backfill (GAD-T100); a371a49 Exam room confirmation and correction: a pending clarification or transcript check shows inline, one at a time, under the question with the answer as recorded (Yes / correct it / repeat for transcripts; reply, decline or fix a typo instead for meaning), with wording that confirming the transcript is not confirming correctness; after each answer, 'Correct a typo in my last answer' (a transcription correction, original kept, never a penalty) and 'I want to change my answer' (a new response event, shown with the exam's revision rule); time running out during a request submits the answer as recorded for human review (GAD-T88); 1d55911 Verification engine and neutral clarification: after each answer, deterministic checks (incomplete sentence, explicit student request, low speech confidence) plus a schema-checked panel vote decide whether the uncertainty could materially change grading; a clarification is worded by a dedicated prompt that forbids technical content, then must pass a no-new-terms check, a no-interpretation-offered check and the LEAKS/SAFE guard, else a template quoting only the student; voice answers get transcript confirmation first; the orchestrator holds judging until the student replies (pending state persisted, resumes after restart), judges the verified text plus the clarification, sends declined/expired/over-budget ambiguity to human review, and exposes Verification, LastAnswer and Notice on SessionStep with hub methods Clarify, ConfirmTranscript, CorrectAnswer and ReviseAnswer; typo fixes are bounded by deterministic correction rules; exam prompt set v3 (GAD-T87); 94bfb23 Response versioning services: every answer is an immutable StudentResponse (original text, modality, Captured) with transcript version 1 and a capture audit event carrying its timings; transcription corrections add versions and update the verified text, meaning clarifications are stored beside the original, substantive revisions are new response rows pointing at what they revise; every state change goes through VerificationMachine as a ResponseVerification row plus an AuditEvent; earlier answered turns are backfilled as Captured originals by a startup service (AddVerification) (GAD-T86); 69b12b8 Demo tour (Gadfly.Tour): starts a real Gadfly.Server under a renamed exe in mock (or --live) mode against a throwaway LocalDB database (--fresh), seeds the demo, and drives the workflow as real users over HTTP, the platform API and the SessionHub (antiforgery sign-in for every role, MOCK banner, access control, teacher setup, API source processing, student exam with good/ambiguous/typo/revision/I-don't-know answers, end and report, mock labelling, AI and human grading, approval, appeal, report export, review, API results, analytics, audit); every stage asserts against the API and database and prints a checklist, unbuilt features SKIP with their ticket by probing hub methods, routes and tables; exit 1 on any failure; docs/TOUR.md (GAD-T105)) | 84f3cc1 |

| GAD-T405 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Owner decision: remove the read-back confirm/correct step from the voice exam. The examiner no longer asks the student to confirm, correct or clarify what was transcribed; whatever speech recognition heard is submitted and graded as-is, and the exam moves straight to the next question/follow-up. Being able to rephrase after hearing the transcript changes the Socratic method (the student gets a second, considered pass instead of a real-time answer). Touches ExamRoom.razor(.cs), VoiceRoom.razor, wwwroot/js/voice-room.js, SessionHub.cs, SessionOrchestrator.cs, ExaminerSpeechWarmup.cs/ExaminerStyle.cs (the read-back speech itself), docs/VOICE.md, docs/EVIDENCE_MAP.md, docs/SCIENCE.md, start-page/consent text. Keep: typed-answer accommodation (GAD-T260) still lets a granted student review/edit before submitting, since that's not voice recognition error correction. Keep: a student can still say 'repeat the question' and 'I don't know'. | GAD-T425 | 2026-11-22 | fix | closed | The Elo-style running mastery estimate (MasteryModel) and the mean judged score still surface as a score: SessionReport.Recommendation (mastered/partial/not-demonstrated) and OverallScore on ReviewList/ReviewSession, and the admin assignments/students consoles fall back to the report OverallScore as the student's score when no final grade exists (AssignmentAdminService/StudentAdminService via AdminPeople.Score). Per ElenchusAtScale Prop. 3.3, Prop. 3.4(b), M9/M10 and Section 4.5 the running estimate must play no part in what is reported and no mean-score aggregation may stand in for the level; show the corroborated objective levels (Level 0 as insufficient evidence) instead, or label the estimate as the examiner's steering aid, never a score | 2878022 |
| GAD-T426 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Word error rate by group (SpeechRecognitionAudit, GAD-T265) is measured against student-checked transcripts, which no longer exist for spoken answers since GAD-T405, so the fairness measure has no reference. Per ElenchusAtScale Section 5.3.1, Appendix A.9 open item and M14: let a consented sample of answers be kept (audio retained only for that sample, per PRIVACY.md and with explicit consent) and transcribed by a human listener in the app, then compute WER and unsure-word rates by group against it. bottleneck: speech-recognition accuracy (and no audio is stored); best mitigation now: the human-listener sample above plus the exam vocabulary hints of GAD-T358 | c75bb8e |
| GAD-T427 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Panel calibration (GAD-T270, PanelCalibrationService) only labels an unaccepted panel provisional; its 0.4 weight still counts. Per ElenchusAtScale Section 3.8 (thresholds decide whether the panel may be used at all, and choose alpha and tau from pilot data), Section 5.4.1 and M13: add a per-exam policy option that sets the panel weight to 0 (human-only) until a calibration is accepted, report recommended weight and disagreement thresholds from the calibration set, report SMD by a pasted unstored grouping (an aggregate can hide a group gap), tune the boundary reconciliation trigger on calibration data, and word the calibrated label so it does not invite deference (Section 5.8.3, Art. 14(4)(b)) | f1d19bd |
| GAD-T428 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Calibration items are posted as raw JSON to POST /grading/calibration with two human levels assembled outside Gadfly; there is no in-app second blind marker. Per ElenchusAtScale Sections 7.2-7.3 (double-blind human marking, calibration set), 2.9.3 (double marking, Meadows & Billington 2005) and M13: let an exam be flagged for double marking so a second examiner grades the same sessions blind to the panel and to the first examiner, then build the calibration set, human-human QWK and the panel-vs-each-marker comparison from those grades in the app | 0307c8b |
| GAD-T429 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | A panel calibration is recorded against a free-text panel name and nothing reopens it when a provider changes the model behind that name. Per ElenchusAtScale Section 6.6 (drift, Pack et al. 2024; correlated change) and Appendix A.8 open item: store the provider model ids each calibration covered, mark it expired (grades provisional again) when any grading-panel member's model id differs, and prompt a re-run of the calibration and the bias probes on a schedule | a03984e |
| GAD-T430 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | The offline objective grader still sees each answer's exam-time stance as a 'Reviewer note' (AiObjectiveGrader.BuildPrompt), and evidence is always in exam order. Per ElenchusAtScale Section 3.8 (online judgment is part of the examiner, not the grader), Section 4.6.2, Section 5.4.2, M1 and M12: drop the stance notes from the grading prompt, and present the evidence in a shuffled order with stable labels so citations still resolve | b2ecaba |
| GAD-T431 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | The same four providers write the questions and grade the answers, and Gadfly does not record which provider's draft became each question, so self-preference cannot be tested. Per ElenchusAtScale Sections 3.8 and 5.4.2 (Panickssery et al. 2024) and M12: record the provider/model whose draft was chosen for each question, and add an analysis comparing each grading member's levels on answers to its own family's questions against others' | 5a386e0 |
| GAD-T432 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | PanelBiasCheck (GAD-T269) exists only as a library class with tests: no CLI command or page runs it, it is never run on human examiners, and no adversarial (prompt-injection) probe exists. Per ElenchusAtScale Sections 4.6.1, 5.3.2 (a paraphrase probe run on humans too would detect a bias panel and human share; Joughin 2010 on articulateness) and 6.8 (adversarial condition; Milani 2025, Chiang 2024): add a gadfly bias-check command (mock-safe, live only with owner approval), a human paraphrase set graded blind, and a spoken-injection probe set | 7ae706f |
| GAD-T433 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Analytics compares panel and human agreement overall but never by student group, and nothing reports score gaps by group. Per ElenchusAtScale Section 5.4.3 (the one fairness check that bears directly on the grade), Section 5.4.1 and Section 3.9 (group-specific s): add an analytics view, with the pasted never-stored grouping and small-group withholding of GazeFlagRates, comparing panel levels, human levels and their difference by group | 94d2913 |
| GAD-T434 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Nothing reports, by group, how often the probing pressure was raised or on which cue, how often the adaptive end-of-answer silence cut a student off, or how often pauses/disconnects hit. Per ElenchusAtScale M15, Section 5.3.3, Section 5.3.4, Section 6.4 and the A.10 open item 'content cues by language' (the hedging, vague-phrase and reason lists are English): add an analytics view of AnswerDelivery cue and pressure rates, answer cut-offs (speech resumed right after the commit) and pause rates per answering minute, by accommodation, typed/spoken and a pasted grouping such as first language | a7edbe6 |
| GAD-T435 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Objective reports show questions, follow-ups and contaminated answers, but not the moves used, the rubric criteria the score covers (criteria left at Level 0 are silently reweighted), or answers excluded as recited or assisted, on the grading and review pages. Per ElenchusAtScale Prop. 3.4(c), M10, Section 3.6 (coverage) and Section 4.6.2: show beside each objective's level the moves asked, criteria reached vs not reached, and every exclusion by reason | 65b3c7a |
| GAD-T436 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Every objective opens with Elicit but its wording is newly generated for each student. Per ElenchusAtScale M2, Section 2.4.3 (Joughin 2010) and Section 4.3.2 (correction 31): let the instructor write or approve one fixed opening question per objective, asked verbatim to every student (generated draft offered for approval, leak-guarded), so the one shared observation is literally shared | cbfe39e |
| GAD-T437 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | The panel-built concept map and per-concept rubric used by the exam-time judge can be the standard of truth without any person reading it. Per ElenchusAtScale Section 4.2, Appendix A correction 35 and Section 6.8 ('requiring approval before a summative examination, has not been made'): block publishing a summative assessment until an instructor has reviewed and approved the concept map and rubric version it runs on, audited, with the approved version recorded on the exam | d5ce940 |
| GAD-T438 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Typed answers (GAD-T260) are stored and labelled but nothing compares them with spoken answers. Per ElenchusAtScale Section 5.7.1 ('What would test it') and the A.10 open item 'the typed group': add an analytics comparison of levels, panel-human agreement and integrity-note rates between typed and spoken answers at the same objective, with the self-selection caveat shown | 72d22b0 |
| GAD-T439 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | The grading queue, grading page and assessment report show the student's name to the human examiner. Per ElenchusAtScale Section 2.9.3 (Meadows & Billington 2005: remove names, train markers, double mark) and Section 5.3.2: add a per-exam anonymous-marking option that shows graders a session code instead of the name until their score is submitted, like blind grading | 49a7021 |
| GAD-T440 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | The claim ledger compares only same-concept claims with word overlap >= 0.15, at most three per claim, ignores the panel's confidence, and an objective with no detection is reported Consistent = true. Per ElenchusAtScale M7, Section 3.4 (a detector's silence is 'no contradiction detected') and Section 4.4: report 'no contradiction detected' instead of consistent, use the recorded confidence, widen candidate selection (embeddings or cross-concept pairs) within the latency budget, and record enough to estimate the detector's false-flag and miss rates on pilot data. bottleneck: panel latency per extra pair; mitigation: the parallel pair checks of GAD-T404 | 69711e5 |
| GAD-T441 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | The ledger has no record of a student withdrawing a claim ('I was wrong earlier'); a retracted claim stays a premise. Per ElenchusAtScale M6, Section 3.4 and Section 4.4: have claim extraction detect explicit retractions, mark the earlier claim retracted (kept for the record), and exclude retracted claims from contradiction checks and Contradiction questions | 423af83 |
| GAD-T442 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Only Apply credits transfer (GAD-T268), but whether its situation is new to the student is asserted by the prompt, not checked. Per ElenchusAtScale M5 and Section 5.2.2 (Table 5.1, M5 'met in design'): add a deterministic check that an Apply question's scenario does not reuse the source passages' examples or a situation the student already discussed (word/embedding overlap), and redraft or record it as extrapolation when it does | edd086e |
| GAD-T443 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | MinSummativeObjectives defaults to 4 as a setting, not an estimate (correction 38). Per ElenchusAtScale Section 3.7 (variance components from a double-marked pilot set the minimum number of objectives), M11 and Section 7.1 (reliability as a function of the number of objectives): add a command or analytics view that estimates the person, objective and rater variance components from double-marked pilot grades and reports the smallest objective count reaching a chosen reliability, to set the policy minimum | 3b1ee49 |
| GAD-T444 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Since GAD-T285 the human scorer cannot reconcile or approve, but the same second person may both reconcile a mandatory disagreement and approve the grade. Per ElenchusAtScale M13, Section 3.8 (a reviewer independent of both judgments), Section 5.9 and correction 47: add an organization option (on by default where two staff exist) requiring the approver to differ from the reconciler, audited like the existing separation-of-duties rule | 53ac889 |
| GAD-T445 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Nothing stops the examiner asking 'how did you arrive at that?', which asks for process information the student may never have attended to. Per ElenchusAtScale Section 2.3.2 (Nisbett & Wilson 1977; Ericsson & Simon 1980: score justifications, not introspection): add a rule to the question prompt and the leak guard against questions about the student's own mental process, and tell the judge to score whether a justification is correct and connected, not whether it reports how the student thought | 773dec1 |
| GAD-T446 | 2026-11-22 | fix | closed | IntegrityExplanations tells reviewers 'People look up or away from a screen to think' and 'Looking away ... is a sign of thinking', and calls off-screen reading 'the most meaningful webcam signal'; docs/SOCRATIC_PLATFORM.md says looking away is 'a well-supported sign of thinking'. Per ElenchusAtScale Appendix A corrections 34 and 42 and Section 2.10.2 (no verified source on gaze aversion while thinking; webcam gaze cannot resolve reading, Rayner 2009): reword to what the evidence supports (looking away has many causes; the camera cannot tell reading from thinking) | 44b8b3c |
| GAD-T447 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | The gaze-rate view (GazeFlagRates) reports look-aways, reading episodes and fades by group, but not absent-face, second-face or changed-face (identity-drift) episodes, nor the GAD-T305 tracking quality score. Per ElenchusAtScale Section 5.6.1 (Yoder-Himes 2022, Buolamwini & Gebru 2018), correction 50 and the A.10 open item 'gaze quality by group': add those episode rates and the quality-score distribution by group. bottleneck: webcam resolution (about 4 degrees of gaze error); mitigation: the per-session calibration and quality score already built | 954a923 |
| GAD-T448 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Nothing measures whether the gaze fade costs honest students anything. Per ElenchusAtScale Section 5.7.3 ('What would test it'): add an analysis comparing, within students, the judged quality of answers during which the screen faded with those during which it did not, reported with the gaze rates; the fade itself is owner decision (c) and is not changed | e0722b5 |
| GAD-T449 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | A student hearing answers through a hidden earpiece and speaking them is not designed against: the camera cannot see an earpiece, the second-voice signal cannot hear one, and only the follow-up question remains, which is untested (hypothesis H1). Per ElenchusAtScale Sections 3.3, 5.5 and 6.8: research and build the best available control, e.g. an ear-visibility check in the get-ready camera step and ledger-based coherence measures for the relay study. bottleneck: webcam resolution and audio pickup cannot detect an in-ear device; best mitigation now: follow-ups that require the principle behind the student's own earlier answer, plus the relay arm of the study | 619845e |
| GAD-T450 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | The student never sees the integrity context recorded about them and can answer it only through an appeal. Per ElenchusAtScale Section 5.9 (accountability: the people affected can see how a grade was reached and contest it): after results are released, let the student see the integrity notes recorded on their attempt with the same plain explanations reviewers get, and respond to them in the appeal flow | 882b79c |
| GAD-T451 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | The planned study needs per-objective panel and human levels, double marks, attempt number and released-feedback state, reconciliation rates and causes, cue and integrity-note counts, typed/spoken mode and a study group, and none of it can be exported as one dataset (analytics counts reconciliations but not their causes). Per ElenchusAtScale Chapter 7 (Sections 7.1-7.3: QWK and SMD, WER by group, score change with and without feedback, rate and causes of reconciliation) and Section 7.5 (data minimization): add a de-identified research export with pseudonymous ids, no audio or video, and small-group suppression | 3be0a39 |
| GAD-T452 | 2026-11-22 | feature | closed | Gadfly cannot tag sessions with a study condition or collect research consent separate from exam consent. Per ElenchusAtScale Sections 7.2 and 7.5 (conditions including a relay arm, feedback withheld vs released across attempts, an adversarial arm; consent) and Section 5.7.3 (the fade tested with a relay condition): add per-assignment study-arm tags and a research-consent step, recorded on the session and carried into the research export; any arm that switches off an owner decision (for example the gaze fade) needs the owner's approval | 242b80f |

| GAD-T471 | 2026-11-22 | fix | closed | StaffNoticeBanner shows 'Your exam is paused' (GAD-T299) but ExamRoom never learns the session is held: VoiceCanAnswer stays true, so voice-room.js keeps the microphone gate open, streams audio to the recognizer and the end-of-answer silence still submits. (found by GAD-T316) | 62fd7f1 |
